metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results (Volume IV) Factsheets: The United Arab Emirates

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet reports results from the PISA financial literacy assessment, which is administered in a complex multistage sampling design of schools and students. The factsheet does not specify the exact student weight variable name(s) or whether replicate weights were used, so the weighting approach cannot be fully audited from the provided text. For PISA analyses, analysts typically apply the provided sampling weights to obtain population-representative estimates for 15-year-olds and to account for clustering by school. Plausible values are used for the financial literacy scale in PISA reporting; however, this factsheet does not describe the PV estimation procedure or any missing-data handling details at the student level.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable here because this document is a descriptive OECD factsheet summarising PISA 2022 financial literacy results (means, proficiency levels, and associations) rather than reporting an explicit student-level predictive model with a stated PV-combining procedure. The factsheet also does not provide a methodological section describing how missing responses were handled in the underlying PISA database processing. Therefore, the PV and missing-data procedures are not transparent in the provided text, representing a reporting gap for this extraction task.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the PISA 2022 financial literacy assessment sample for the United Arab Emirates (students in sampled schools who participated in the financial literacy domain). The factsheet does not describe additional exclusions beyond the standard PISA sampling and assessment participation procedures.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume IV factsheet summarises the first participation of the United Arab Emirates in the PISA 2022 financial literacy assessment. Financial literacy was measured with a computer-based test administered to sampled students, with students split so that one group took financial literacy plus either mathematics or reading, while the other group took the core PISA subjects; both groups received 120 minutes total testing time. The factsheet reports the UAE mean financial literacy score (441) relative to the OECD average (498), proficiency-level distributions (39% below Level 2; 7% at Level 5), and how much of the variation in financial literacy is explained by mathematics and reading performance (about 80% in the UAE). It also describes associations between financial literacy levels and self-reported financial behaviours, parent discussions, and exposure to financial education at home and school. The document is descriptive and does not provide the underlying PV estimation, missing-data strategy, or any ML model evaluation details.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD PISA factsheet that reports descriptive statistics and associations from the PISA 2022 financial literacy assessment rather than an empirical ML study with a specified predictive target, model, and performance metrics. As a result, fields related to ML techniques and structured predictive findings are intentionally empty. The provided text also lacks technical details on PV combining and missing-data handling, which are typically documented in the broader PISA technical reports rather than in country factsheets.
